verdict.root_cause: Callers of cart hang on gRPC connection acquisition, not on cart's work. Frontend's CartService/GetCart client span stalls ~418s and checkout's equivalent stalls ~360s with a connection-draining error before a retry succeeds in ~12ms, while every cart server span and its Redis HGET complete in under 3ms [tr_4dc2d066e40d]. The wait, not an error, is what breaks the request: frontend-proxy ingress simply times out at 15s and shows no sustained error elevation, only a late spike at 19:18:31 [tr_5fa950d65469]. Impact is confined to cart-touching journeys; ad, product-catalog, recommendation and product-reviews are normal [tr_4dc2d066e40d]. No change record exists for cart or frontend in the queried window [tr_7fdf875bc59d][tr_951a7c59e85c], so this looks like cart-side connection handling (serving endpoints going away / connections being torn down or exhausted) making callers wait rather than fail. I blame cart as the dependency whose reachability degraded, with frontend and frontend-proxy merely the places the latency surfaced.
verdict.reasoning: The trace evidence localises all missing wall time to the client side of the frontend-to-cart and checkout-to-cart gRPC calls, with cart server handling fast whenever reached [tr_4dc2d066e40d]; that rules out cart compute or Redis saturation and rules out proxy/frontend self-time. Proxy error metrics show no sustained error step, consistent with timeouts rather than fast failures [tr_5fa950d65469]. The failure is therefore 'the service waited on a dependency', i.e. dependency_latency, and the dependency is cart. Change logs are empty for both cart and frontend over the queried window, so no deploy, config edit or flag flip is implicated [tr_7fdf875bc59d][tr_951a7c59e85c]. Restarting/recycling cart pods and their client connections is the fix that would clear stuck connection acquisition; no change exists to revert.
open_questions: Cart's own unfiltered logs were never read - only a 'drain' substring search, which matched nothing [tr_201a537ff8d9]; whether cart logged connection-limit, shutdown or unreachability errors is unknown, and a partition or freeze of some cart replicas is not excluded.
Cart span metrics returned no samples in either window, so no cart-side resource, replica-count, connection-count or churn data exists [tr_fc027628e1ec].

Change history for cart and frontend was queried from the incident timestamp forward, not the hours preceding it [tr_7fdf875bc59d][tr_951a7c59e85c], and frontend-proxy, checkout and other services were never queried for changes.
The connection-draining error text appears in a checkout trace [tr_4dc2d066e40d] but its origin (cart replica shutdown, mesh/LB config, pool limit) is unresolved.

alternatives.root_cause: A subset of cart replicas is stopped or network-isolated while their sockets still accept, so callers hang to their deadlines and retries that land on healthy replicas succeed.
alternatives.why_not: Callers eventually reach a fast-completing cart server span within the same trace and a retry succeeds in ~12ms [tr_4dc2d066e40d], which is more consistent with slow connection acquisition than a fully silent process; cart's own logs were never read unfiltered to confirm silence [tr_201a537ff8d9].

alternatives.root_cause: Cart has exhausted its connection, thread or file-descriptor capacity, so new gRPC connections queue for minutes while in-flight requests complete in milliseconds.
alternatives.why_not: No cart resource, connection-count or replica metrics were collected at all [tr_fc027628e1ec], so exhaustion is an untested hypothesis; the observed mechanism from the caller's side remains waiting on a dependency.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating cart's container resets its gRPC listener and connection state. Observable in new frontend traces: CartService/GetCart client spans fall from hundreds of seconds to the sub-3ms range already seen on cart server spans, the connection-draining error on checkout's GetCart stops appearing, and user_view_cart and user_checkout_multi complete well under the 15s proxy ingress timeout. Measure by re-running the frontend trace query over a 10-minute window after the recreate and comparing max GetCart client-span duration.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, 2-6 minutes after the recreate, frontend or checkout GetCart client spans still stall for tens of seconds while cart server spans stay sub-3ms - that points to a network partition or mesh/LB endpoint staleness, which reconnect_service would address but it is unavailable. Inconclusive if no cart-touching traces are sampled; cart emits no span metrics [tr_fc027628e1ec], so traces are the only confirmation channel.
proposal.risk: If the mechanism is network- or mesh-side rather than cart process state, the restart does nothing and converts slow cart journeys into hard failures during the recreate. It is irreversible and destroys the live process state needed to diagnose a connection-limit or exhaustion condition - cart's unfiltered logs were never read [tr_201a537ff8d9]. If a leak refills, the symptom returns.
proposal.blast_radius: cart only, during the recreate. Callers seeing resets: frontend and checkout [tr_4dc2d066e40d]; surfacing onward to frontend-proxy and load-generator cart journeys. Cart's in-process state is cache only; cart contents persist in Redis.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts across frontend-proxy and frontend plus the load generator indicate user-facing failure, not a single quiet latency warning. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the edge-level cause among the six downstream services is unmeasured, so specialists are warranted.
